title: Filing-event meta-signal drift: post-first_avail reaction to norm-relative arrival lateness, event-anchored 63-session books with a lexicographic placebo control (announcement-timing reaction lineage)
mechanism: WHO is the constrained actor: the filer arriving late to the tape — its filing event lands into a market that has already been waiting past the filer's own seasonal habit; the constrained counterparty is the attention-constrained investor who processes the filing's CONTENT (the numbers) but not its META-SIGNAL (arrival time relative to the filer's own norm and to peers), so the lateness information must be impounded through slower trading over the following sessions. WHY the effect exists: at the event instant the lateness is jointly public with the content; disclosure-timeliness evidence shows announcement-window abnormal returns are already ordered by report lag (Chambers-Penman 1984), but event-window underreaction decays over roughly one quarter (Bernard-Thomas 1989 horizon precedent; Hong-Stein 1999 gradual diffusion), and no published result prices the arrival-time RESIDUAL as a drift conditioner rather than an announcement-window level effect. H2 claims precisely the residual: conditional on a filing having JUST arrived, names that arrived LATE relative to their own seasonal norm drift DOWN over the following quarter and names that arrived EARLY drift UP — the claim is about the diffusion of the meta-signal, not about any accounting quantity: the exposure carries no fundamental field whatsoever (a deliberate structural contrast with H1's slow characteristic book: H1 prices the persistent state, H2 prices the reaction to the event). WHAT observable measures it: the first_avail stamp itself (the availability evidence, per the P0 rule that the vintage/submission timestamps ARE the evidence) gates a 63-session event window; within it, exposure = -own_z of the arriving period (clock V10-T2); names without a recent event hold CASH. WHEN it must fail: (i) if the deterministic placebo control — the identical event book with legs assigned by lexicographic ticker order, carrying ZERO timing information — reproduces the anchor at >= 0.5x expectancy same-sign, the performance is generic post-filing event exposure (announcement-season beta), not lateness diffusion, and the family dies; this clause also fences H2 off from any post-earnings-announcement-drift rescue claim, because content-driven event drift would show up in the placebo, not in the anchor's edge OVER the placebo; (ii) if pooled D2 Spearman |rho| > 0.20 vs any of the nine veto entries measured on the event-active cohort; (iii) if > 90% of expectancy comes from names whose final bar falls within 21 sessions of entry (terminal death-event mechanics, not timeliness); (iv) any inherited Stage-A gate failure per the ex-ante margins. WHICH control kills the convenient explanation: the lexicographic-ticker placebo event book — same events, same windows, same grid, same costs, information-free leg assignment; 'any post-filing drift' and 'filing-season beta' are exactly the explanations it detects.
falsifiable_prediction: Directional and falsifiable: among the event-active cohort at each 21-session decision, the sector-centered median split of exposure = -own_z predicts relative returns over the following 63 sessions — the early-arrival half outperforms the late-arrival half in at least 2 of 3 folds after base band costs, with (a) long-short expectancy > 0, (b) position PF >= 1.10, (c) the SHORT half (late arrivals) carrying the majority of the spread: short-leg expectancy <= -0.5 x long-leg expectancy (the meta-signal is a late-arrival penalty, per the timeliness asymmetry), (d) risk-matched excess vs SPY positive in >= 2 folds and overall alpha > 0, (e) the lexicographic placebo event book NOT reproducing the anchor: placebo expectancy magnitude < 0.5x anchor expectancy in the anchor's direction, placebo alpha not positive-when-anchor-negative, and the placebo never outperforming the anchor on expectancy, (f) the cohort_z neighbour (V10-T3) supporting same sign — if only the neighbour works, the market reads lateness vs peers and not vs own habit, and the terminal records the own-norm frame as wrong, (g) anchor-vs-neighbour Spearman rho < 0.95 measured pre-selection (both read z scores of the same lag; correlated but not identical), and (h) pooled Spearman |rho| <= 0.20 vs all nine veto entries on the event-active cohort at D2. If any of (a)-(h) fails, the family is rejected and filing-event meta-signal drift is declared untradable on this cohort at these costs; every failure mode is a successful research outcome.

entry_exit_fills.fill_check_preregistered: a fill references only names with a bar at the fill session; a missing bar means the order does not exist — no silent substitute pricing (p3 dead-name book semantics)
entry_exit_fills.exit_preregistered: a held name exits when (a) its event age exceeds 63 sessions at a decision (to CASH with cost), (b) a new first_avail replaces g* and the exposure refreshes to the new arriving period's z at the next decision, or (c) its series ends — exited at its LAST recorded close on its final session, the delisting return carried by the price series; no synthetic penalty, no synthetic continuation
entry_exit_fills.no_survivorship_resubstitution: a dead name is never replaced by a successor entity's series; books re-form only at decision sessions from the event-active eligible set
entry_exit_fills.weights: equal-weight within the long and short halves after sector-centering, CASH absorbs residual; min 1 non-CASH leg per scored decision, min 30 scored decisions overall, min 5 scored decisions per fold; declared non-vacuity: timing rows by eff_year inside the folds run 440,638 (2018) down to 154,522 (2025), so event density supports the abstain floor — A9 verifies measured decision counts before selection
entry_exit_fills.hysteresis: leg membership persists while the name stays event-active (63 sessions) and refreshes only on a replacing event — the event book's declared churn control to hold turnover inside the frozen 6.0x/yr ceiling; if A9 measures ceiling breach, the proposal is BLOCKED pre-score, recorded honestly

arms.role: causal/placebo control designed to refute the mechanism-specific explanation
arms.score: the IDENTICAL event book (same event cohort, 63-session windows, grid, sector-centering, weights, costs) with legs assigned by LEXICOGRAPHIC TICKER ORDER within the sector-centered event cohort — a deterministic, information-free rank
inputs: ticker identifiers (not a market or filing input)
price series for inherited eligibility and fills only
arms.direction: lexicographically first half long, second half short (no economic direction by construction)
arms.mechanism_refuted_if_reproduced: the mechanism claim is that the ARRIVAL-TIME RESIDUAL diffuses into returns after the event. If the information-free placebo reproduces the anchor at >= 0.5x expectancy same-sign, the performance is generic post-filing event exposure — announcement-season beta, event-window drift of any content — and the timing meta-signal carries nothing; the family dies as mechanism-mistitled. This control also structurally separates H2 from any post-earnings-announcement-drift (content) claim: content-driven event drift reproduces in the placebo, not in the anchor's edge OVER the placebo
arms.differs_from_anchor_in_data_space: the control consumes ONLY the event calendar (first_avail membership) and the ticker string — the z score is entirely absent — while the anchor's legs are a function of own_z; the two ranks are constructed from disjoint information sets (placebo: calendar+identifier; anchor: calendar+own_z), and the placebo's expectancy is expected near zero by construction

exposure_definition: Per entity e and decision session t on the inherited 21-session grid (PIT gate = 00:00 UTC of t): (1) g*(e,t) = the filer-period group of e with the LARGEST first_avail(g) < gate(t); event age a(e,t) = number of cohort trading sessions between the first session whose gate is strictly after first_avail(g*) and t; e is EVENT-ACTIVE iff a(e,t) <= 63 sessions; otherwise e holds no rank (weight 0, CASH). (2) z = own_z(g*) exactly as frozen in p0_v10_observable_manifest.json ([first_lag - own prior-only seasonal median] / (1.4826*MAD), min_hist_own = 4); null rows excluded-with-reason, never fallen back to raw lag. (3) exposure(e,t) = -z for event-active names; undefined for all others. HIGHER exposure = early arrival vs own norm = LONG; LOWER = late arrival = SHORT. (4) Book: demean exposure within sector across the event cohort, split at the event-cohort median: long the positive half, short the negative half, equal weight, CASH absorbs; decisions with < 6 event-active ranked names abstain. D2 ranking contract: pooled Spearman rho of exposure(e,t) vs each of the nine veto entries computed on the EVENT-ACTIVE cohort subset on the same dates; pooled |rho| <= 0.20 required against all nine (63-session prior return, semivariance share, vol level, WC-stock intensity, Goodwill/Assets, F1 accrual flow, depletion-runway interaction, Cash/Assets, sector-exposure form).

novelty_declaration.lineage_statement: the mechanism is new to this factory and to the proposal literature as expressed here: announcement-timeliness research measures announcement-WINDOW level effects of report lag (Chambers-Penman; Kross-Schroeder); conditioning a drift book on the norm-relative arrival-time residual — content-blind, placebo-fenced — is a construction of this proposal; the multi-vintage submission machinery that makes the event gate PIT-evidenced only exists since V10 P0
novelty_declaration.measured_decorrelation_required: |rho| <= 0.20 pooled vs every forbidden ancestor and all nine veto entries, measured at D2 on the event-active cohort; anchor-vs-neighbour correlation allowed nonzero (shared z inputs) but must be < 0.95; the falsification-by-control cluster (ledger E.2) is answered by a zero-information placebo that isolates exactly the event-calendar explanation

literature: Chambers, A.E. and Penman, S.H. (1984), 'Timeliness of Reporting and the Stock Price Reaction to Earnings Announcements', Journal of Accounting Research 22(1) — announcement-window abnormal returns ordered by report lag; the level effect H2 claims to extend into drift.

Kross, W. and Schroeder, D.A. (1984), 'An Empirical Investigation of the Effect of Quarterly Earnings Announcement Timing on Stock Returns', Journal of Accounting Research 22(1) — early announcers outperform late announcers; grounds the direction.
Givoly, D. and Palmon, D. (1982), 'Timeliness of Annual Earnings Announcements: Some Empirical Evidence', The Accounting Review 57(3) — lateness carries information about news quality.
Trueman, B. (1990), 'Theories of Earnings-Announcement Timing', The Accounting Review 65(2) — strategic timing; the constrained actor's incentive.

Bernard, V.L. and Thomas, J.K. (1989), 'Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Delayed Price Response or Risk Premium?', Journal of Accounting Research 27(Supplement) — the 1-3 month event-horizon measurement precedent for the 63-session window.

Hong, H. and Stein, J.C. (1999), 'A Unified Theory of Underreaction, Momentum Trading, and Overreaction in Asset Markets', Journal of Finance 54(6) — gradual information diffusion; grounds why the meta-signal impounds over a quarter.

Doyle, J.T. and Magilke, M.J. (2009), 'The Timing of Earnings Announcements: Institutional and Aggregate Implications', The Accounting Review 84(2) — timing choice transmits information beyond the numbers.
McLean, R.D. and Pontiff, J. (2016), 'Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?', Journal of Finance 71(1) — post-publication decay caveat: a null result is a legitimate outcome.
